Anand Counsel for Opposite Party :- Uma Kant Gupta,G.A.

Hon'ble Suresh Kumar Gupta,J.
Heard learned counsel for applicants, learned counsel for the opposite party no.1 and the learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material available on record.

The present application under Section 482 Cr.P.C. has been filed with the prayer to quash the impugned order dated 21.12.2021 passed by IX Additional Civil Judge (Junior Division)/ J.M., Rae Bareli in complaint case no.1095 of 2020, under Sections 498A, 323, 504 IPC and Section 3/4 Dowry Prohibition Act.

sentences.text: At the very outset, learned counsel for applicants has submitted that the dispute between the parties has been amicably settled and the parties have entered into a compromise in terms of settlement agreement dated 17.4.2023.
No grievance has left between the parties.
Learned counsel for opposite party no.1 does not dispute the correctness of the submission made by learned counsel for applicant or the correctness of the documents relied upon by him.
He submits that opposite party no.1 has no objection, if the proceedings in the aforesaid are quashed.

From perusal of the record, it is apparent that the parties have entered into compromise and have settled their dispute amicably and it is highly doubtful if the ingredients of the offence as alleged are made out.

Considering the facts and circumstances of the case and the submissions advanced by learned counsel for the parties regarding the compromise entered into between the parties and taking all these factors into consideration cumulatively, the compromise between the parties be accepted and further taking into account the legal position as laid down by the Apex Court in the cases of B.S.
Joshi Vs. State of Haryana; 2003 (4) SCC 675 as well as State of Madhya Pradesh vs Laxmi Narayan and others; AIR 2019 SC 1296, the entire proceedings of the aforesaid case is hereby quashed.
